text: Which side of the table do I sit on as the Dervish?
answer: The Dervish player sits next to the west edge of the map (§3).

text: Do I need to punch every counter to play Fall of Khartoum?
query: RETURN string::contains(rule:r3_preparation.statement, 'punch out only the counters needed');
answer: No. Select a scenario and punch out only the counters needed to play it; the rest can be punched, sorted and stored later (§3).

text: Which direction is my 'home' edge?
answer: The Dervish player sits at the west edge and the Anglo-Egyptian player opposite him at the east edge (§3).
note: §3 only says where the players sit. It defines no 'home edge'; where units enter is set by each scenario (§9).

text: How far can this cavalry move?
answer: Up to its printed movement allowance, 15 for the 21 Lancers, paying the terrain cost of each hex it enters (§5.11, §2.3).

text: What does it cost to move into a hut hex?
answer: Look it up on the Terrain Effects Chart (§5.11). The cost is printed on the mapsheet, not in the rules text, so the corpus does not have it.
note: Terrain Effects Chart cells are not in the manual text. The query shows that no cost is recorded and that the missing chart is logged as an open gap.

text: Do I have to move every unit?
answer: No. You may move as many or as few of your units as you like each movement phase (§5.12).

text: Can I just leave the artillery where it is?
query: SELECT VALUE kind FROM rule WHERE section = section:`5.12`;
answer: Yes. Moving is optional for every unit (§5.12).

text: What stops me moving further?
query: SELECT VALUE section.num FROM rule WHERE actions CONTAINS action:move AND kind IN ['limit', 'obligation'] AND string::starts_with(section.num, '5');
answer: Your movement allowance, the terrain costs you pay from hex to hex (§5.11), and enemy zones of control, which stop you on entry (§5.12, §5.26, §5.43).

text: My unit sat still last turn. Can it move double this turn?
answer: No. Movement points may never be accumulated from turn to turn (§5.13).

text: Can my leader give his leftover MP to the infantry he's with?
answer: No. Unused movement points may not be transferred to other units (§5.13).

text: I have 2 MP left and the next hex costs 3. Do I keep the 2?
answer: No. You cannot pay for the hex, and the unused 2 MP are lost at the end of the turn (§5.11, §5.13).

text: Can my gunboat carry the Lancers across the river?
answer: No. Gunboats may not carry land units. The only exception is the Friendlies ferry of §5.21.
note: See needs_movement.md: the corpus has a load capability only for the Friendlies, so fn::allowed returns NONE ('unstated') for every other land unit.

text: When can the Friendlies cross?
answer: Only after the Dervish east bank unit, Isa Zachneih, has been eliminated (§5.21).

text: How many turns does the ferry take?
answer: Three Anglo-Egyptian turns: load, sail to a Nile hex next to the west bank, disembark (§5.21 a–c).

text: Can the Friendlies move on the turn they get off the boat?
answer: Yes. On the third turn they disembark and move normally, paying the normal terrain cost for the first hex they enter (§5.21c).

text: Does the gunboat have to stay put while unloading?
query: RETURN string::contains(rule:r5_21_friendlies_ferry.params.steps[2].text, 'the gunboat may also move normally');
answer: No. The gunboat may also move normally on the turn the Friendlies disembark (§5.21c).

text: Is the loaded gunboat breaking the 'gunboats stack alone' rule?
answer: No. A Friendlies unit loading onto (stacking with) a gunboat is the stated exception to 'gunboats may not stack with any other unit' (§5.51, §5.21).

text: Why would I bother ferrying the Friendlies?
answer: It adds Friendlies strength on the west bank. The cost: each Friendlies unit eliminated on the west bank gives the Dervish 3 VP instead of 1 on the east bank (§9.14, citing §5.21).

text: Can infantry wade onto an island hex across the Nile?
answer: No. Land units may never enter a Nile River hex (§5.22). The only exception is the Friendlies ferried by gunboat (§5.21).

text: Can anything besides gunboats go into the river?
query: SELECT VALUE in FROM entry WHERE out = terrain:nile_river AND allowed = true;
answer: No. Only gunboats may enter and move along Nile River hexes. The sole exception is Friendlies carried aboard a gunboat under §5.21 (§5.22).

text: Can my Baggara fall back into the walled city?
answer: No. Of the Dervish units, only the Khalifa, the three artillery units and the Taiasha may enter the walled city (§5.23).

text: Can the Khalifa leave the city?
answer: Yes. Units may enter and exit the walled city, but only through a gate or breach hexside (§5.23).

text: Can my Highlanders climb the wall?
answer: No. British infantry may enter the walled city, but only through a gate or breach hexside, never across a wall hexside (§5.23).

text: Can the Friendlies help storm the city?
answer: No. Gunboats and Friendlies are the two Anglo-Egyptian unit types that may not enter the walled city (§5.23, §6.52).

text: Which Dervish units can garrison the inner city?
query: SELECT VALUE in FROM entry WHERE out = location:walled_city AND allowed = true AND in.faction = faction:dervish;
answer: Only the Khalifa, the three Dervish artillery units and the Taiasha units, the Khalifa's bodyguard (§5.23).

text: Which way is upstream?
answer: Upstream is against the current. The arrows printed in the Nile show the direction of the current (§5.24).

text: My gunboat went 10 hexes downstream. Can it come back 2 upstream?
answer: No. Once a gunboat moves even one hex upstream, its upstream allowance (10 for an old gunboat) caps its whole move for the turn, and 10 + 2 = 12 is over it (§5.24).
note: Part B's bracket ('Yes, if the total stays within 10') is confusing: 10 down plus 2 up totals 12, which exceeds the cap of 10.

text: If I move one hex upstream, can I still use the 16?
answer: No. One upstream hex makes the upstream allowance (10) the maximum for that turn (§5.24).

text: Can I go 15 downstream and then stop?
answer: Yes. Moving only downstream, an old gunboat may use up to 16; units never have to spend their full allowance (§5.24, §5.11).

text: Can I reposition my fort?
answer: No. Dervish forts may not move in any way once placed (§5.25).

text: I moved next to an enemy unit. Can I keep going?
answer: No. A unit must stop immediately when it enters an enemy zone of control (§5.26, §5.43).

text: Can I build a zariba anywhere I like?
expect: only as displayed on the mapsheet
answer: No. Zariba hexsides may only be built in the positions printed on the mapsheet (§5.3).

text: Which units can build it?
query: SELECT VALUE in FROM capability WHERE out = action:construct_zariba AND allowed = true;
answer: Anglo-Egyptian infantry units: British, Egyptian and Sudanese battalions. Cavalry, artillery and Maxims cannot (§5.3).
note: Whether the Royal Engineers or the Friendlies count as 'Anglo-Egyptian infantry' is not settled; see the open questions s5_3_op_engineers_build and s5_3_op_friendlies_build.

text: How long does it take?
expect: one Anglo-Egyptian player turn (begin and end adjacent)
answer: One full Anglo-Egyptian player turn: the unit must begin and end that player turn adjacent to the hexsides (§5.3).

text: Can my builders still shoot back on the Dervish turn?
answer: The ban names only offensive fire and melee attack during the turn of construction. Defensive fire is not mentioned, so the manual does not settle it (§5.3).

text: Does one battalion build the whole Zariba?
expect: all Zariba hexsides to which it is adjacent
answer: No. It builds only the Zariba hexsides it is adjacent to (§5.3).

text: Which side do I have to be on?
answer: The Nile side of the Zariba hexsides (§5.3).

text: How do we remember who's building?
answer: Mark constructing units with a blank counter (§5.3).

text: Does Kitchener alone pin enemy spearmen?
answer: No. Anglo-Egyptian leaders are the one kind of unit with no zone of control (§5.41).

text: Does a gunboat stop infantry walking along the bank?
answer: No. Gunboats exert a ZOC only against enemy gunboats (§5.41), and no ZOC extends out of a Nile hex anyway (§5.44).

text: My battalion got disrupted. Can the enemy walk past it?
answer: Yes. Disrupted units have no ZOC (§5.41).

text: Do Dervish leaders have a ZOC?
answer: Yes. Every unit except Anglo-Egyptian leaders exerts a ZOC, Dervish leaders included (§5.41).

text: Do forts have a ZOC?
answer: Yes, even when unoccupied (§5.41, §5.44, §6.54).

text: Does entering or leaving a ZOC cost extra?
answer: No. Entering or leaving an enemy ZOC costs no movement points (§5.42).

text: I'm stuck next to the enemy. Can I leave next turn?
query: SELECT VALUE kind FROM rule WHERE actions CONTAINS action:withdraw_from_zoc AND section = section:`5.43`;
answer: Yes. In your next movement phase you may withdraw (§5.43).

text: Can I slide from one enemy's ZOC directly into another's?
answer: Yes, in your next movement phase. You must then stop again in the new ZOC (§5.43).

text: Can I move through two ZOC hexes in one turn?
answer: No. You must stop in the first enemy ZOC you enter and may move no further that turn (§5.43).

text: Does the enemy across the khor stop my movement?
answer: No. ZOCs do not extend across a khor (§5.44).

text: My Dervish unit is in a fort. Does the British unit next to it stop me leaving?
answer: No. ZOCs do not extend into a fort, so the unit inside is not in the enemy ZOC (§5.44).

text: My unit is next to an empty enemy fort. Am I in its ZOC?
answer: Yes. ZOCs extend out of a fort even if it is unoccupied (§5.44, §6.54).

text: Do the Taiasha behind the wall pin my troops outside?
answer: Yes. ZOCs extend from a walled city hex into an adjacent hex outside the city across a wall hexside (§5.44).

text: Do my troops outside pin the defenders inside the wall?
answer: No, not across a wall hexside. Across a breach hexside, ZOCs extend both ways (§5.44).

text: Can units in a hut village be pinned?
answer: No, but they pin others. ZOCs extend out of a hut hex but not into it (§5.44).

text: Can troops inside the Zariba be ZOC-locked from outside?
answer: No. ZOCs extend out of the Zariba across a Zariba hexside but not into it: in the historical scenario, and in the campaign game once it is built (§5.44).

text: Does a gunboat ZOC the riverbank?
answer: No. ZOCs do not extend out of a Nile River hex; a gunboat's ZOC acts only against enemy gunboats (§5.44, §5.41).

text: How many battalions can I put in a hex?
answer: Four. No more than four units may occupy a hex; leaders and gunboats are the exceptions (§5.51).

text: Does Kitchener count toward the 4?
query: LET $s = fn::stack_check([unit:egyptian_battalion_sample, unit:egyptian_battalion_sample, unit:egyptian_battalion_sample, unit:egyptian_battalion_sample, unit:kitchener]); RETURN [$s.legal, $s.counted_units];
answer: No. All leaders are free stacking, on top of the four-unit limit (§5.51).

text: Can two gunboats share a hex?
answer: No. Gunboats may not stack with any other unit, other gunboats included (§5.51).

text: Can my column pass through an already-full hex?
answer: Yes. You may move through friendly units at no extra cost; the stacking limit applies only at the end of the movement phase and during combat (§5.51).

text: Can an advance after combat overstack?
answer: No. The stacking limit applies during combat, and §7.6 has the Dervish advance only 'up to the stacking limit' (§5.51, §7.6).

text: Can Mulazmin and Jehadia stack? They're both green.
answer: No. Units of different Dervish tribes may not stack together, even if they are the same color (§5.52).

text: Can I stack Baggara with Jaalin?
answer: No. They are different tribes (§5.52).

text: Can Osman Digna join a stack of Baggara?
answer: No. A Dervish leader may stack only with units of his own command; Osman Digna's are the Hadendowa (§5.53, §9.112).

text: Can Sheik El Din stand alone?
answer: Yes. Leader units are not required to stack (§5.53).

text: Can Sheik El Din stack with Jehadia?
answer: Yes. The Jehadia belong to his (green) command, together with the Mulazmin (§5.53).

text: What does '3E' on my counter mean?
query: SELECT VALUE name FROM ONLY formation WHERE designation = '3E' LIMIT 1;
answer: It is the brigade designation: 3rd Egyptian Brigade (§5.54).

text: Do I get a bonus for keeping the brigade together?
answer: Yes. A stack with brigade integrity gets +1 on its fire combat die roll if all four fire at the same hex (§5.54).

text: If one battalion was eliminated, do the three survivors still get it?
answer: No. Brigade integrity requires all four infantry battalions of the brigade in the same hex (§5.54).

text: If I split fire between two hexes, do I lose it?
answer: Yes. The +1 applies only if all four battalions fire at the same enemy-occupied hex (§5.54, §6.15).

text: Can I mix battalions from two brigades to get the bonus?
query: RETURN string::contains(state:brigade_integrity.definition, 'all four infantry battalions belonging to any Anglo-Egyptian infantry brigade');
answer: No. All four battalions must belong to the same brigade (§5.54).

text: What's my total die modifier with integrity?
query: RETURN fn::fire_drm({firer: faction:anglo_egyptian, direct: true, integrity: true});
answer: +2: the normal +1 Anglo-Egyptian direct fire bonus plus +1 for brigade integrity, before terrain (§5.54, §6.24).

text: Does it apply on defensive fire?
answer: Yes. Integrity counts 'in any combat phase', defensive fire included (§5.54).

text: What is Kitchener's movement allowance?
answer: 15, printed on his counter (0·0·15) (§5.11, §2.3).

text: How far can the Maxim battery move?
answer: Its printed movement allowance is 12 (Maxim Batt. 6·1·12) (§5.11, §2.3).

text: What is the 32 Battery's movement allowance?
What is the Royal Engineers' movement allowance?
How far can an Egyptian infantry battalion move?
answer: The sample Egyptian battalion has movement allowance 8 (9·5·8) (§5.11, §2.3).

text: What is a Danagla camel unit's movement allowance?
What is the Sultan's movement allowance moving upstream?
answer: 12, the smaller number of its 12/18 movement allowance (§5.24).

text: What is the Sultan's movement allowance moving only downstream?
answer: 18, the larger number of its 12/18 movement allowance (§5.24).

text: How far can an old gunboat move with the current?
answer: 16 hexes, as long as it moves no hex upstream that turn (§5.24).

text: Can an old gunboat move 6 hexes downstream and 4 back upstream in one turn?
answer: Yes. Gunboats may combine both directions; with any upstream movement the total may not exceed the upstream allowance of 10 (§5.24).

text: What is the Lancers' movement allowance at night?
answer: 7. All Anglo-Egyptian movement allowances are halved at night, rounded down (15 → 7) (§8.1).

text: Do Dervish units move less at night?
answer: No. Only Anglo-Egyptian movement allowances are halved at night; a Danagla camel unit still moves 12 (§8.1).

text: How far can an Egyptian battalion move on a night turn?
answer: 4: half of its 8 (§8.1).

text: What is Kitchener's movement allowance at night?
answer: 7: half of 15, rounded down (§8.1).

text: How far can an old gunboat move upstream on a night turn?
answer: 5. Gunboats are Anglo-Egyptian units, so their allowance is halved too: 10 upstream becomes 5 (§8.1, §5.24).

text: Can a gunboat stack with infantry?
answer: No. Gunboats may not stack with any other unit. The only exception is the Friendlies ferry (§5.51, §5.21).

text: Can Kitchener ride along on a gunboat?
answer: No. Leaders are free stacking, but gunboats may not stack with any other unit (§5.51, §5.21).

text: What does it cost in movement points to move through my own units?
answer: Nothing extra. You may move through friendly units at no additional movement point cost (§5.51).

text: May I end my move with five infantry battalions in one hex?
answer: No. No more than four units may occupy a hex at the end of the movement phase (§5.51).

text: Can Osman Digna join a full stack of four Hadendowa?
query: LET $s = fn::stack_check([unit:osman_digna, tribe:hadendowa, tribe:hadendowa, tribe:hadendowa, tribe:hadendowa]); RETURN [$s.legal, $s.counted_units];
answer: Yes. Leaders stack free on top of the four-unit limit, and the Hadendowa are his command (§5.51, §5.53, §6.51).

text: Can my cavalry ford the Nile?
answer: No. Land units may never enter a Nile River hex (§5.22).

text: Can a Dervish gunboat move along the Nile?
answer: Yes. Gunboats, Dervish or Anglo-Egyptian, are the units that may enter and move along Nile River hexes (§5.22).

text: Can my units enter the walled city through a breach?
answer: Yes. Units enter or exit the walled city through a gate or breach hexside (§5.23).

text: Can Dervish artillery enter the walled city?
answer: Yes. The three Dervish artillery units are among the few Dervish units allowed in (§5.23).

text: Can the Taiasha enter the walled city?
answer: Yes. The Taiasha are the Khalifa's bodyguard and may enter (§5.23).

text: Can Osman Digna enter the walled city?
answer: No. The Khalifa is the only Dervish leader allowed in (§5.23).

text: Can Jehadia units enter the walled city?
answer: No. Only the Khalifa, the Dervish artillery and the Taiasha may (§5.23).

text: Can the Maxim battery enter the walled city?
answer: Yes. Any Anglo-Egyptian unit that can get there may enter, except gunboats and Friendlies, through a gate or breach (§5.23).

text: Can Kitchener enter the walled city?
answer: Yes. Anglo-Egyptian leaders are not excluded; like every unit they must use a gate or breach hexside (§5.23). This is how a British leader reaches the Mahdi's Tomb (§9.14).

text: Can a gunboat enter the walled city?
answer: No. Gunboats are excluded from the walled city (§5.23).

text: Into how many hexes does a unit's zone of control extend?
answer: Into its six adjacent hexes (§5.41).

text: Do the Royal Engineers exert a zone of control?
answer: Yes. Every unit except Anglo-Egyptian leaders does (§5.41).

text: Does my artillery battery have a zone of control?
answer: Yes. Only Anglo-Egyptian leaders lack one (§5.41).

text: Does a Dervish gunboat exert a ZOC against my gunboats?
answer: Yes. Gunboats exert a ZOC, but only against enemy gunboats (§5.41).

text: Does a ZOC extend through a breach into the walled city?
answer: Yes. ZOCs extend both ways across a breach hexside (§5.44).

text: Does my ZOC extend into the walled city through a gate?
answer: No. ZOCs extend out of a walled city hex across a gate hexside, but not into it (§5.44).

text: Do units inside the walled city exert a ZOC out through a gate?
answer: Yes. ZOCs extend out of (but not into) a walled city hex across a gate hexside (§5.44).

text: Can an enemy ZOC reach my units in a building hex?
answer: No. ZOCs extend out of, but not into, a hut or building hex (§5.44).

text: Do my riverbank troops exert a ZOC into the Nile against gunboats?
answer: No. ZOCs do not extend into or out of a Nile River hex; only gunboats exert ZOCs on gunboats (§5.44, §5.41).

text: Does a khor block zones of control in both directions?
answer: Yes. ZOCs do not extend across a khor at all (§5.44).

text: In which scenario can the Anglo-Egyptian player build the Zariba?
answer: In the campaign game. In the historical scenario it is already built (§5.3).

text: Do I have to build the Zariba in the historical scenario?
answer: No. The Zariba trench and thorn hedge hexsides are built and in place in the historical scenario (§5.3).

text: What are unbuilt Zariba hexsides in the campaign game?
answer: Clear terrain, unless the Anglo-Egyptian player constructs them (§5.3).

text: Can a battalion building the Zariba melee attack that turn?
answer: No. The constructing unit may neither fire offensively nor melee attack during the turn of construction (§5.3).

text: Can the 21 Lancers build Zariba hexsides?
answer: No. Only Anglo-Egyptian infantry units construct the Zariba (§5.3).

text: Can the Maxim battery build the Zariba?
answer: No. It is not an infantry unit (§5.3).

text: Can a British infantry battalion build the Zariba?
answer: Yes, in the campaign game, by beginning and ending the Anglo-Egyptian player turn adjacent to Zariba hexsides on their Nile side (§5.3).

text: In which direction may the Friendlies be ferried?
answer: From the east bank of the Nile to the west bank (§5.21).

text: Can a Dervish gunboat carry Dervish units?
answer: No. Naval transport is not allowed; the only exception is the Anglo-Egyptian Friendlies ferry (§5.21).

text: Can the Sultan ferry a Friendlies unit?
answer: Yes. Any Anglo-Egyptian gunboat may carry a Friendlies unit from the east bank to the west bank once Isa Zachneih is eliminated (§5.21).

text: Can four Baggara units stack together?
answer: Yes. Units of the same tribe may stack, up to four (§5.51, §5.52).

text: Can the Khalifa stack with his Taiasha?
answer: Yes. The Taiasha are the Khalifa's bodyguard (§5.23), and a leader may stack with units of his command (§5.53).

text: Can Osman Digna and Sheik El Din stack together?
answer: No. A Dervish leader that stacks may stack only with units of his own command (color). Sheik El Din is a unit of the green command, not of Osman Digna's, and the reverse holds too (§5.53).
note: See needs_movement.md: fn::stack_check checks a Dervish leader only against non-leader units, so two leaders of different commands come out legal.

text: How many battalions of a brigade must be stacked together for brigade integrity?
answer: All four infantry battalions of the brigade, in the same hex (§5.54).

text: What does it cost to enter or leave the Zariba?
answer: +2 movement points to cross one of the two end hexsides that connect to the Nile, which are the only way in or out (§9.233, referenced by §5.3).

text: Does it cost extra movement points to enter or leave a friendly fort?
answer: No. There is no additional movement point cost to enter or leave a friendly fort (§6.54).

text: Which sections' rules govern stacking?
answer: The stacking rules are §5.51–5.53, plus §6.51, where Dervish leaders 'stack free'.

text: Which rules are exceptions to the four-unit stacking limit (directly or as exceptions to its exceptions), and in which sections?
query: SELECT id, section.num AS section FROM rule:r5_51_limit.{..+collect}(<-exception_to<-rule);
answer: Leaders stack free and gunboats stack alone (§5.51). The Friendlies ferry is in turn an exception to the gunboat rule (§5.21).

text: Which sections refer the reader to §5.4 (zones of control)?
answer: §5.12 (movement is limited by enemy ZOCs) and §5.26 (stop on entering an enemy ZOC).

text: Which sections cite the Friendlies ferry rule §5.21?
answer: §5.22 (Nile), §5.51 (gunboat stacking), §6.52 (Friendlies) and §9.14 (west-bank Friendlies victory points).

text: Which tribes share Sheik El Din's command?
answer: The Mulazmin and the Jehadia (§5.53, §9.112).

text: Which units belong to the green command?
query: RETURN array::flatten((SELECT VALUE array::concat(<-member_of<-tribe, <-leads<-unit) FROM command_group WHERE color = 'green'));
answer: The Mulazmin and Jehadia tribes and their leader, Sheik El Din (§5.52, §5.53).

text: Which tribe may Osman Digna stack with?
answer: Only the Hadendowa, his command (§5.53, §9.112).

text: What is the transitive class chain of the Royal Engineers?
answer: Royal Engineers → combat unit and land unit → unit. They are not classed as infantry, which is why their Zariba eligibility is open (§6.53, §5.3).

text: Which ZOC boundaries let a ZOC out but not in?
query: SELECT VALUE id FROM zoc_boundary WHERE out_of = true AND into = false;
answer: Fort, wall hexside (from the city outward), gate hexside, hut and building hexes, and the Zariba hexsides (§5.44).

text: Which rules does the Friendlies ferry make an exception to?
answer: The ban on naval transport (§5.21), the ban on land units in Nile hexes (§5.22) and the gunboats-stack-alone rule (§5.51).

text: Which rules are exceptions to 'all units exert a ZOC'?
answer: Gunboats exert a ZOC only against enemy gunboats, and disrupted units have none (§5.41). Anglo-Egyptian leaders are excluded in the rule itself.

text: Which unit types never exert a zone of control?
query: SELECT VALUE in FROM capability WHERE out = action:exert_zoc AND allowed = false;
answer: Anglo-Egyptian leaders (§5.41). Disrupted units also lose theirs, but that is a state, not a unit type.

text: Which actions does constructing the Zariba prohibit?
answer: Offensive fire and melee attack, during the turn of construction (§5.3).

text: Which infantry types can form a brigade with brigade integrity?
query: SELECT VALUE in FROM is_a WHERE out = unit_class:ae_infantry;
answer: British, Sudanese and Egyptian infantry (§5.54).

text: Which Anglo-Egyptian unit types may enter the walled city?
query: SELECT VALUE in FROM entry WHERE out = location:walled_city AND allowed = true AND in.faction = faction:anglo_egyptian;
answer: All of them except gunboats and Friendlies: infantry, cavalry, Camel Corps, artillery, Maxims, Royal Engineers and leaders, through a gate or breach (§5.23).

text: In which phases is normal movement performed?
answer: In each player's own Movement Phase (§4, §5).

text: May a unit building the Zariba fire defensively?
answer: The manual is silent. §5.3 forbids only offensive fire and melee attack during the turn of construction.

text: Can the Royal Engineers build the Zariba?
answer: The manual does not say. §5.3 names 'any Anglo-Egyptian infantry unit' and never says whether the Royal Engineers count as one.

text: Can a Friendlies unit build the Zariba?
answer: Unstated. The Friendlies are Anglo-Egyptian and fight as infantry, but §5.3 does not say whether they count for construction.

text: Why must Zariba builders begin and end the turn adjacent when the Royal Engineers can demolish on the turn they arrive?
answer: The manual does not explain the difference. §5.3 requires begin-and-end adjacency, while §6.53 lets the Engineers move adjacent and finish at the end of the same player turn.

text: May a gunboat leave the Nile and enter a land hex?
answer: The manual never says so outright. §5.22 says only gunboats may enter Nile hexes, not that gunboats must stay in them (common sense says they do).

text: Which Dervish units count as cavalry for retreat purposes?
answer: Not stated. Apart from the sample Danagla camel counter, the manual never says which Dervish units are cavalry or camel units (§2.3, §7.5).

text: Can the Friendlies brigade get brigade integrity?
answer: Not settled. §5.54 names only British, Sudanese and Egyptian infantry; the Friendlies are called a brigade (§6.52) but are none of these, so presumably not.

text: Do leaders count toward the stacking limit when the Dervish must advance after melee?
answer: The manual is silent. §7.6 says 'up to the stacking limit', and §5.51 makes leaders free stacking, but neither says how the two combine.

text: Can Yakub stack with the Jaalin?
answer: The text does not say. §9.112 groups Yakub, Sherif and Ali Wad Helu with the Baggara, Jaalin, Danagla, Kehena and Degheim without saying which leader commands which tribe; the counter colors decide (§5.53).
note: fn::stack_check([unit:yakub, tribe:jaalin]) returns legal: true, which says more than the manual does; see needs_movement.md.

text: What color is the Baggara command?
answer: The manual names a color only for the green command (Mulazmin, Jehadia). The other colors are on the counters, not in the text (§5.52).

text: Does a gunboat's ZOC reach an enemy gunboat across a river chain, or affect units on Nile islands?
query: SELECT VALUE id FROM open_question WHERE refs CONTAINS section:`5.41`;
answer: The manual is silent. §5.41 says only that gunboats exert a ZOC against enemy gunboats; it says nothing about chains (§10.2) or islands.
note: Part C 16. The corpus has no open_question for it yet; see needs_movement.md.

text: Does a fort counter count as one of the four units in its hex?
query: SELECT VALUE id FROM open_question WHERE refs CONTAINS section:`5.51`;
answer: The manual does not say. §5.51 excepts only leaders and gunboats from the four-unit limit, while §6.54 speaks of units 'stacked inside the fort', as if the fort were terrain.
note: fn::stack_check counts a fort as a unit (5 = fort + 4 Baggara is illegal), which settles a question the manual leaves open; see needs_movement.md.

text: Can my unit move through a hex holding only a disrupted enemy unit?
query: RETURN [fn::allowed(tribe:baggara, action:overrun_leader), (SELECT VALUE id FROM action WHERE string::starts_with(name, 'move through'))];
answer: Unstated. §5.51 allows moving through friendly units, and a disrupted enemy has no ZOC (§5.41), but no rule covers moving through enemy units. The only stated case is a Dervish unit passing through a lone Anglo-Egyptian leader (§6.51).
